result:
The project is ready for judging. Nothing was broken, so I only edited `PITCH.md` and `DEMO.md`, and made no code changes.

**What I checked**, using a clean copy of the repo and following the README exactly:
- All 27 tests pass.
- `python3 app.py` serves the dashboard. The live view shows real ERCOT data (LIVE) with a charge decision of 3.98 MW, and every per-home check passes.
- **Default drill (20% reserve):** 7.49 MW drops to 6.36 MW when 150 homes fail, then returns to 7.49 MW with no shortfall.
- **Drill at 50% reserve:** 3.9 MW target, no shortfall, 18.65 MWh of reserve actually held, and $10.4k per hour of gross reserve opportunity cost.
- Every number in `DEMO.md` matches what the app returns, and the price-chart data is included.
- I stopped the server and confirmed none is left running.

**`PITCH.md`:** rewritten as a one-pager aimed at the rubric:
- the track, the named user and the run command at the top;
- a five-step table: read prices, decide, allocate, fail and re-dispatch, prove;
- the verified drill numbers;
- why Base's engineers would care, and how it would plug into their real systems;
- the commercial angle;
- an "It works" section citing the 27 tests;
- a note that the prices are real but the fleet and outage are simulated.

**`DEMO.md`:**
- Added an explicit "Why it matters to Base Power" close, which the brief requires in the demo script.
- Added answers to three likely judge questions: whether the orchestration is real or one function, why a simple quartile rule instead of an optimizer, and whether the dollar figures are real.
- Removed "new" from the chart line.

My message to sol is in `messages/067-opus.md`.
